statement.p: Find the length of the curve x = -\left(4+5t\right),\quad y = 3t-4, z = 4-3t, for 2 \le t \le 3.

p.em: (Think of second way that you could calculate this length, too, and see that you get the same result.)

static.solution: \hbox{Length} = \int_2^3 \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2 + (z'(t))^2}\,dt = \int_{2}^{3} \sqrt{(-5)^2+(3)^2+(-3)^2}\,dt = \sqrt{43}. This is the length of a straight line from the point (-14,2,-2) to (-19,5,-5).
